title: The Dangerous road over the hill
subtitle: 安全预防 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 安全预防（人与自然·灾害防范·安全与预防）
meta: 主题语境：安全预防（人与自然·灾害防范·安全与预防）　|　核心词汇：dangerous　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dangerous 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1976 the researcher wrote of ① a dangerous road over the hill in the paper, and everybody in the lab said at once that it was ② more dangerous than the one named there the year before. Three terms on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the researcher, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the dangerous ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most dangerous road over the hill anybody in the lab had ever seen, or so the paper for February 1970 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too dangerous to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the student who had come to help; the dangerous ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the tube at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a dangerous plan for the crossing, and said that no student in his right mind would call it ⑥ as dangerous as the plan for the crossing they had once had in the old lab. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was dangerous or not, and he said so.

By 1983 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the paper. What the line asked for was ⑦ something dangerous, and nothing besides. The student from the next lab called the whole plan ⑧ quite dangerous; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the paper kept the names of the dangerous ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1986, for the whole place, she wrote of another dangerous road over the hill in the same paper, and the work, which took two terms, seemed ⑨ more dangerous than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most dangerous plan for the crossing in the whole lab, she said in 1988, was the one she could never quite name; the dangerous ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 危险（前置定语 a dangerous road over the hill：1976 年研究员在研究报告里记下的那件危险的那条路）
B. adj. 危险／有风险（比较级 more dangerous than：文中两处，一处比翻山的那条路，一处比预想）
C. adj. 危险／有风险（最高级 the most dangerous：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 危险（表语 too dangerous to do：母亲觉得它太危险，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 有风险（前置定语 a dangerous plan for the crossing：叔叔把整件事称作一桩有风险的计划）
F. adj. 有风险（同级比较 as dangerous as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩渡河的计划相比）
G. adj. 有风险（后置定语 something dangerous：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 有风险（受程度副词修饰 quite dangerous：那位学生的评价）

items.q: a dangerous road over the hill
the most dangerous road over the hill anybody
a dangerous plan for the crossing
The most dangerous plan for the crossing in

answers.why: dangerous 意为“危险”，1976 年研究员在研究报告里记下的是“一件危险的那条路”，此处作前置定语 a dangerous road over the hill。
dangerous 意为“危险”，此处用比较级 more dangerous than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
dangerous 意为“危险”，研究报告上 二月 那行字说它是实验室里最危险的一件，故用最高级 the most dangerous road over the hill。
dangerous 意为“危险”，母亲认为这件东西“太危险了，谁也用不上”，too dangerous to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
dangerous 意为“有风险”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩有风险的计划”，此处作前置定语 a dangerous plan for the crossing。
dangerous 意为“有风险”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩渡河的计划一样有风险”，同级比较用 as dangerous as。
dangerous 意为“有风险”，研究报告上那半行字要的是“有风险的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something dangerous。
dangerous 意为“有风险”，邻实验室来的那位学生认为这套计划“相当有风险”，quite 修饰原级 dangerous。
dangerous 意为“有风险”，1986 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要有风险”，故用比较级 more dangerous than。
dangerous 意为“有风险”，母亲 1988 年说的是“整个实验室里最有风险的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most dangerous plan for the crossing。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1976 年，研究员在研究报告里记下了一件危险的那条路。（a dangerous road over the hill）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更危险。（more dangerous than …）
母亲觉得它太危险，谁也用不上。（too dangerous to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩有风险的计划。（a dangerous plan for the crossing）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩渡河的计划一样有风险。（as dangerous as …）
到了 1983 年，研究报告上只剩半行字：要的是一件有风险的东西。（something dangerous）
answers: In 1976 the researcher wrote of a dangerous road over the hill in the paper.
Everybody said it was more dangerous than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too dangerous to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a dangerous plan for the crossing.
He said nobody would call it as dangerous as the plan for the crossing they had once had.
By 1983 the paper asked for nothing but something dangerous.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 dangerous 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1976 the researcher wrote of a dangerous road over the hill in the paper, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most dangerous road over the hill in the lab, or so the paper says.
My mother thought it too dangerous to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a dangerous plan for the crossing, and nobody argued with him.
The student from the next lab called the plan quite dangerous, and everybody laughed.
The dangerous ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
